The articles listed hereunder are approved under Reference 90. Articles classified in Section I to X of the Customs Tariff, concession code 903403L, the remainder classified in Sections XI to XX of the Customs Tariff, concession code 903844C is applicable. 1. Unrestricted Approvals (provided such articles are designed exclusively for religious use) Alms dishes bearing an inscription or other marking to indicate that they are for religious use in places of worship Altar book rests Altar bread Altar cruets and altar flagons for wine and water Altar linen in sets, burses and veils, fair linen cloths and altar frontals embroidered with religious emblems Altar vases bearing an inscription or other marking to indicate that they are for religious use in places of worship Altars Asperges bowls and sprinklers Aumbries Brass bells Brass butter lamps Brass offering bowls Brass religious statues Calendars, church, designed solely as aids to worship ie, those listing church festivals, Saints' days, fast days, liturgical colours, or other items of purely religious significance Candle extinguishers Chalice spoons Chalices Chauka and memorial (yahrzeit) candles Chanuka Menorah (Chanukiah) candelabra and oil lamps Ciboria Communion trays and plates. Covers for trays and plates are free of duty when imported therewith (excluding plastic substitutes) Communion glasses (excluding plastic substitutes) Communion tables Cope clasps Crosses and crucifixes, of any size and any material including precious metals, not being articles for wear Cruet dishes Ecclesiastical vestments, including cassocks (whether choir or clerical or for lay readers), exclusively for wear at church services Etrog boxes Figures not less than 25cm in length for crucifixes Font Ewers Fonts Havdalah candle holders and spice boxes Incense boats, nails and spoons Jewish praying shawls exclusively for wear at synagogue services. These are known as tallithin or taleism (plurals for tallith) and worn by male Jews at synagogue services Lamps, sanctuary and sanctum, including glasses and stands Lavabo bowls Lecterns Mezuzot (singular-mezuzah) Missal stands Monstrances Oil stocks, being cylindrical containers for use in sick communion sets Patens Pulpits Processional crosses, crucifixes and torches purification dishes and finger bowls for use at the altar Pyxes Religious banners, medals and medallions Rosaries and chaplets Scapulars and scapular medals Seder plate Sick communion sets Stations of the Cross sets Statues of religious subjects, not less than 60 cm in height Stoups Tabernacles Thuribles, and thurible stands Torah Timonim crowns, shields and pointers (yadim) Viaticum sets Wafer boxes Wooden prayer beads 2(a) Approvals, restricted as to use The articles listed hereunder are approved under Reference 90 if the NZ Customs Service at the port of admission is satisfied from evidence produced that they are ordered by or on behalf of the authorities of an institutional place of worship (including the chapels of hospitals, orphanages, religious communities, and the like) for installation therein. Altar bells Altar candlesticks and candelabra Church bells including electronic church bells Figures less than 25 cm in length for crucifixes Organs, including seats and amplifying apparatus (tone cabinets) imported therewith excluding those classified in Tariff item 9207.10.01 Statues of religious subjects less than 60 cm in height (b) Exclusions Articles imported for installation outside the precincts of a place of worship, for installation in a dwelling (including those of religious communities), or by a dealer for holding in stock, are subject to duty at normal rates. There are no suitable means whereby the duty paid in such cases may be refunded if at some later date the articles are installed within the confines of a place of worship.
